thesis: Apparent rule changes may be state changes in an extended representation, without being simple or discoverable.

ideas.statement: Effective state and repertoire updates can be combined into fixed dynamics over an extended state.
New operational vocabulary matters through cost and transfer, whereas syntactic novelty alone supplies no new capability.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: A hidden switch can explain a source changing from repetition to inversion.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: External inputs and growing memory must be accounted for; existence of a metarule does not supply an identification algorithm.
